evals.name: builds-from-the-design-without-regrilling
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage. .harness/csv-export/artifacts/design.md is approved: it adds a CSV export of the runs list as a new server route reusing the existing list query, with D1 'stream the rows' instead of 'build the file in memory'.
evals.expected_output: The stage reads design.md, sweeps the code with Explore agents, and writes plan.md and phase files that build the streaming route. It asks the user nothing the design already answers, and its only question is the Approve? gate.
expectations: design.md is read before any other file is written.
An Agent call with an Explore sweep is made before plan.md is written.
plan.md has a ## Phases section holding a digraph, and one phases/phase-N.md exists per node.
A step implements D1 as streaming.
anti_expectations: Asks the user whether to stream or build in memory
Presents alternative approaches for the user to choose between
Writes plan.html or starts a viewer

evals.name: every-change-is-a-diff
evals.prompt: plan: rename the `owner` field on Invoice to `issuedBy` across the API, the store and the two React forms that write it. The design is approved at .harness/rename-owner/artifacts/design.md.
evals.expected_output: Phase files whose steps show each change as a ```diff fence under a line naming the file and range: removed lines with -, added lines with +, a hunk header when line numbers are known. Existing code appears only as - lines, or as a labelled pattern block when the step imitates it.
expectations: Every step that changes a file carries a ```diff block.
Each diff label names the file and the line range, e.g. src/models/invoice.ts:12-18.
A new file is a diff of + lines only.
Every diff line opens with +, -, @@ or a space.
anti_expectations: Shows a 'before' block and an 'after' block for one change instead of a single diff
Describes a one-line edit in prose ('change owner to issuedBy on line 14') with no diff
Leaves an existing-code block with no label saying why it is on the page

evals.name: contradiction-goes-to-the-user
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage. The approved design.md says the webhook sender already retries through a shared `retry()` helper and the plan should raise its limit. In this repo the sender has no retry at all.
evals.expected_output: The stage finds the code disproves the design, shows the user the evidence with a file:line, recommends a new decision, and asks. After the answer, design.md states the new decision and plan.md's ## Design corrections records the change.
expectations: An AskUserQuestion names the contradiction and cites the sender's file:line.
plan.md has a ## Design corrections section recording what the design assumed, what the code shows, and what the user decided.
design.md states the corrected decision, and is edited only after the user answered.
anti_expectations: Plans a change to a retry helper that does not exist
Silently picks a new approach without asking
Edits design.md before the user answered

evals.name: no-finish-without-approval
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage for the approved design at .harness/node-timeout/artifacts/design.md. When shown the plan, I'll answer Revise and ask for phases 2 and 3 to be merged.
evals.expected_output: The first Approve? question gets Revise. The stage merges the phases in the files, re-runs its self-review, says what changed, and asks Approve? again. The stage finishes only after an Approve answer.
expectations: AskUserQuestion with header Approve? is called at least twice.
After the revision, the ## Phases digraph and the phase files show the merged phase.
The done command with --artifact plan=artifacts/plan.md runs only after an Approve answer.
anti_expectations: Treats the Revise answer as approval
Asks Approve? the second time without saying what changed
Renumbers phases in a way that leaves a phase file and the digraph out of step
